name: Section-heading-lockup
purpose: The repeatable in-page heading that sits above one section of content (a board, a table, a panel) — as distinct from Page-header-lockup's page-level <h1>. Composed ENTIRELY from Layout-utilities (l-row/l-stack), Eyebrow, Cards' arrow-link atom, Badge and Button — no new visual vocabulary, only arrangement. Itinerary row 116 (Layer 2, NO-ARTEFACT-CLASS at mint; PROPOSED here, not ruled).

props.name: arrangement
props.$note: Three arrangement variants drawn in the reference: A bare label (the Template-dashboard shape), B label + trailing arrow-link action, C eyebrow + heading + count badge + a two-button action group. Structural variance, a VARIANTS-axis prop (same class-C6 reading as Tags' `type` prop, s142-D1).

variants.name: label
variants.use: Bare section label above a board or panel — the default, most sections need nothing more.

variants.name: label-action
variants.use: A section whose full contents live elsewhere (e.g. 'Recent activity' + a View all link).

variants.name: eyebrow-badge-actions
variants.use: A section that also needs to show a live count (e.g. pending approvals) and offer filter/export actions.

tokens.heading: canon/type.css .t-cm-section-label (20/500) or .t-ed-heading-4 (20/28/300) composite — never a raw declaration
tokens.action-link: text/default + primary/background/default (tip) via Cards.reference.html's a.arrow, unmodified
tokens.badge: badge/background + rag/text/on-light via Badge.reference.html's standalone form
tokens.$note: Every token above resolves through the ATOM's own manifest; this organism binds nothing new. The lock-up's own CSS (`.l-row`/`.l-stack`, borrowed from Layout-utilities) is flex arrangement only.

responsive.$status: PROPOSED at #210 wave-6 (not ruled) — reflow verified in a real browser at 3 widths.
responsive.rule: The Layout-utilities l-row primitive wraps by default (flex-wrap:wrap); this lock-up declares no container-type or width of its own — the action group and eyebrow fall onto their own line when the PAGE (or an ancestor) narrows, exactly as demonstrated at 320px in the reference.
responsive.$note: s210-D3 discipline: the lock-up declares no width of its own; the enclosing page or container gives it one.

livesInside: Any content region needing a labelled header
mustNotNeighbour: Page-header-lockup in the same slot (one is the page <h1>, the other an in-page <h2>/<h3> — never both naming the same region)

accessibility.structure: The heading is an <h2> (or <h3> if nested under another section) — never the page's sole <h1>; heading order is the consuming page's responsibility.
accessibility.focus: Every borrowed atom (arrow-link, button, badge) keeps its OWN :focus-visible ring — the organism adds no new focusable element and no new focus style.

antiPatterns: Re-drawing the heading, eyebrow, arrow-link or button CSS instead of composing the existing atom
Giving the lock-up a fixed width or its own container-type — the enclosing page/container owns that
Using this lock-up for the page's own <h1> — that is Page-header-lockup's job
More than one action group per heading row — pick label-action OR eyebrow-badge-actions, not both
